section: President of India - election, qualifications, term, impeachment; executive, legislative, financial, judicial powers

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the absolute veto of the President of India?
o: Keeping a Bill pending without deciding on it
Withholding assent to a Bill
Returning an Ordinary Bill for reconsideration once
Overriding a Bill by a higher majority in Parliament
accepted.x: Absolute veto means withholding assent to a Bill. It may apply to Private Members’ Bills and Government Bills when the Council of Ministers has resigned before assent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the three forms of presidential veto by their operative effect: withhold, return or keep pending.

accepted.s: The absolute veto of the President may ordinarily be exercised in respect of which of the following?
o: Private Members’ Bills and Government Bills when the Cabinet has resigned before assent
Money Bills alone
Constitutional Amendment Bills alone
Bills passed by a State Legislature only
accepted.x: The absolute veto involves withholding assent and is relevant to Private Members’ Bills and Government Bills when the Cabinet resigns before assent.
accepted.tq: Match the veto with the specific class of Bills to which it applies, while rejecting extreme alternatives such as ‘alone’.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the suspensive veto of the President:
1. It involves returning a Bill for reconsideration once.
2. If the Bill is passed again, the President must give assent.
3. It is available in respect of Money Bills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: A suspensive veto permits the President to return an Ordinary Bill once for reconsideration. If Parliament passes it again, assent becomes mandatory. This veto does not apply to Money Bills.
accepted.tq: Find the single wrong statement by testing the important Money Bill exception.

accepted.s: With reference to the pocket veto of the President of India, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It can be exercised only for a period of six months.
It permits the President to return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
It keeps an Ordinary Bill pending without any constitutional time limit for decision.
It is a veto that can be overridden by a two-thirds majority of Parliament.
accepted.x: Pocket veto means keeping a Bill pending without taking a decision. The Constitution prescribes no time limit for the President to act in this manner, and it applies to Ordinary Bills.
accepted.tq: Separate pocket veto from suspensive veto by focusing on the absence of a constitutional time limit.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the qualified veto in the Indian constitutional system?
o: It involves the possibility of overriding the veto through a specified stronger majority.
It can be overridden by a higher majority.
It is recognised as a veto available to the President of India.
It is conceptually different from an absolute veto.
accepted.x: Qualified veto is an overridable veto by a higher majority, but it is not available to the President of India. Therefore, its recognition as an Indian presidential power is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Identify the exception by separating a general constitutional concept from the power actually available in India.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the case of a Money Bill, the President may either give assent or withhold assent.
2. The President may return a Money Bill for reconsideration under the suspensive veto.
3. The President is constitutionally bound to give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The President may assent to or withhold assent to a Money Bill but cannot return it for reconsideration. Under the Twenty-Fourth Amendment, assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill is mandatory.
accepted.tq: Use the Bill-type distinction: Money Bills cannot be returned, whereas Constitutional Amendment Bills require assent.

accepted.s: The constitutional requirement that the President must give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill is associated with the:
o: Seventy-Third Amendment
Forty-Fourth Amendment
Twenty-Fourth Amendment
Forty-Second Amendment
accepted.x: The Twenty-Fourth Constitutional Amendment made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitutional Amendment Bill duly passed by Parliament.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-number trap by linking the specific constitutional change to the correct amendment.

accepted.s: The Eleventh Constitutional Amendment of 1961 is associated with which of the following changes?
o: Removal of nominated members from the Vice-Presidential electoral college
Providing for election of the Vice-President by State Legislatures
Ending the joint-meeting method for the election of the Vice-President
Introduction of direct election to the office of Vice-President
accepted.x: The Eleventh Amendment ended the earlier joint-meeting method and provided for election of the Vice-President by the members of both Houses of Parliament.
accepted.tq: Test the amendment by identifying the precise institutional procedure it altered, not the broader office concerned.

accepted.s: Jagdeep Dhankhar’s resignation as Vice-President in July 2025 and the subsequent election of C. P. Radhakrishnan are relevant primarily to which constitutional provisions?
o: Articles 61 and 72
Articles 65 and 68
Articles 74 and 75
Articles 52 and 53
accepted.x: Articles 65 and 68 deal respectively with the Vice-President acting as President and the filling of a vacancy in the office of Vice-President. The July 2025 resignation therefore invoked these provisions.
accepted.tq: Use the office-function pairing: identify the Articles dealing with acting arrangements and a Vice-Presidential vacancy.

accepted.s: C. P. Radhakrishnan became Vice-President of India after the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar. This was described as the:
o: First mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
Second mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
Third mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
Fourth mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President
accepted.x: The resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar and the election of C. P. Radhakrishnan constituted the third mid-term vacancy in the office of Vice-President.
accepted.tq: Treat the ordinal number as a direct quantitative fact and reject nearby sequential distractors.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the tenure of the President of India:
1. The Constitution prescribes no limit on the number of terms that a person may serve as President.
2. India follows an informal convention limiting the President to two terms.
3. The two-term limit is expressly imposed by a constitutional amendment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The Constitution does not prescribe a term limit for the President, although an informal convention of two terms is discussed. No constitutional amendment expressly imposes such a limit.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a constitutional rule from an informal convention and reject the amendment trap.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the comparison concerning presidential term limits?
o: The United States permits only one presidential term, whereas South Korea permits two five-year terms.
The United States limits a President to two terms, whereas South Korea provides for a single five-year term.
Both the United States and South Korea prescribe two presidential terms.
Both the United States and South Korea prescribe a single five-year presidential term.
accepted.x: The Twenty-Second Amendment of the United States limits a President to two terms. South Korea follows a single five-year presidential term.
accepted.tq: Handle comparison questions by checking both parts of the pair rather than recognising only one correct country.

accepted.s: N. Sanjiva Reddy is associated with which one of the following distinctions?
o: Being the first Vice-President of India
Being the first nominated President of India
Being the only President of India elected unopposed
Being the first President elected directly by the people
accepted.x: N. Sanjiva Reddy holds the distinction of being the only President of India elected unopposed. He was elected President in 1977.
accepted.tq: Use the unique-distinction clue and reject options that confuse presidential and vice-presidential election methods.

accepted.s: President Droupadi Murmu promulgated the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026. What change did the Ordinance provide?
o: Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, excluding the CJI
Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 37 to 40, excluding the CJI
Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, including the CJI
Increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 31 to 33, excluding the CJI
accepted.x: The 2026 Ordinance increased the number of Supreme Court judges from 33 to 37, with the Chief Justice of India excluded from this count.
accepted.tq: Separate the numerical change from the counting exception relating to the Chief Justice of India.

accepted.s: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 was gazetted on:
o: 16 July 2025
8 June 2026
accepted.x: The Ordinance was gazetted on 16 May 2026. The other dates relate to reports or commentary rather than the gazette date.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the official notification date from later reporting and criticism dates.

accepted.s: The President addresses both Houses of Parliament assembled together at the commencement of the Budget Session under:
o: Article 88
Article 85
Article 87
Article 123
accepted.x: Article 87 provides for the President’s special address to both Houses assembled together at the commencement of the first session after each general election and the first session of each year, including the Budget Session context.
accepted.tq: Use the Article-number distinction among provisions dealing with parliamentary sessions, participation and ordinances.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Election method of the President of India — United States
Impeachment procedure of the President of India — Ireland
Election method of the President of India — Ireland
Impeachment procedure of the President of India — South Korea
accepted.x: The method of election of the President of India was borrowed from Ireland, whereas the impeachment procedure was borrowed from the United States.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure borrowing pair and guard against swapping the sources of election and impeachment.

accepted.s: Epuru Sudhakar is associated with which constitutional issue?
o: Appointment of the Governor
Financial emergency under Article 360
Election of the Vice-President
Review of the pardoning power
accepted.x: The 2006 Epuru Sudhakar case concerned judicial review of the exercise of the pardoning power. It is associated with the constitutional limits on clemency decisions.
accepted.tq: Link the case name with its distinctive constitutional power instead of the office or emergency provisions.
